attributes.action: No Community Should Be Erased from Staffordshire Libraries
attributes.additional_details: Public libraries are places of learning, inclusion and community. Reports that Pride Month displays have been removed from Staffordshire libraries have raised concerns about LGBTQ+ visibility in public spaces. We believe libraries should be free to recognise communities protected under the Equality Act 2010. The Government should ensure local authorities cannot restrict displays that promote equality, diversity and inclusion.
attributes.background: Protect equality, inclusion and representation in publicly funded libraries by ensuring local authorities cannot ban displays recognising protected characteristics, including LGBTQ+ communities, during awareness events such as Pride Month.

rejection.details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors
